stories.primary_headline: Minister raises concern over rising number of maternal deaths

primary_source.headline: Minister raises concern over rising number of maternal deaths
primary_source.content: Chitradurga: The rising number of maternal deaths despite the availability of modern facilities in hospitals is a matter of concern as maternal and infant mortality can be reduced if medical officers closely monitor the health of pregnant women, Health and Minority Welfare Minister U T Khader said.He was speaking at a progress review meeting of the health and minority welfare departments held at the deputy commissioner's office auditorium on Friday.Kannada vocabulary, dialects, folk knowledge and literary heritage must be preserved: Minister UT KhaderEven if pregnant women show minor signs of complications, they should immediately be shifted to the district hospital by ambulance. They should be admitted to hospitals at least three days before delivery. Doctors should ensure the health of both mother and child during childbirth. If serious complications arise, they should be referred to the district hospital. Awareness programmes must also be conducted in rural areas, he said.Four maternal deaths have been reported in the current year. The women died due to high blood pressure and lung infections. Compared to last year, the maternal mortality rate in the district has declined by 50%, District Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) Officer D M Abhinav said.Khata campaign sees 11,000 visitors in four weeks'Visit PHCs'The minister directed taluk health officers to visit and inspect primary health centres under their jurisdiction at least three times a month.During every visit, officers should identify deficiencies and problems and take steps to address them and introduce necessary improvements, he said.Meetings involving local MLAs, organisations and hospital staff should be held at least once a month. Hospitals should not have to wait for government funds for renovation, cleaning of toilets or painting. It is the responsibility of taluk health officers to seek assistance from local MLAs and organisations to renovate and maintain hospitals, he said.Minority schoolsResidential schools and colleges under the Minority Welfare Department should give importance to sports and extracurricular activities alongside quality education. It was encouraging that SSLC results in the district's APJ Abdul Kalam, Morarji Desai and Maulana Azad residential schools had exceeded 90%, he said.MLA K C Veerendra, Urban Development Authority chairperson M K Tajpeer, Deputy Commissioner S Ramya, Assistant Commissioner K Kantaraj, Health Department district nodal officer Ranganath, District Health Officer M C Sunil Kumar, District Guarantee Schemes Implementation Authority chairperson R Shivanna, and vice-chairperson D N Mailarappa, were present.Process e-khata applications in two days, open 10 PSK-style centres in Bengaluru: D K ShivakumarOutside prescriptionsIn another progress review meeting held at the Hiriyur City Municipal Council hall on Friday, Health Minister U T Khader warned government hospital doctors of strict action if they prescribe medicines that patients are required to purchase from outside."The government is supplying all necessary medicines to patients. Asking them to buy medicines from outside amounts to exploiting the poor. This should not continue," he warned.

stories.primary_headline: Amit Shah sounds poll bugle in Uttarakhand; promises UCC in all BJP governed states

primary_source.headline: Amit Shah sounds poll bugle in Uttarakhand; promises UCC in all BJP governed states
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Sounding the poll bugle in Uttarakhand, Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Friday said that the BJP will slowly implement Uniform Civil Code in all states governed by the saffron party. He called for the party leaders to ensure that the party wins 65 seats in the upcoming Assembly elections.Addressing a rally in Dehradun on the occasion of Uttarakhand’s State Foundation Day, Shah said that after the implementation of the UCC in Uttarakhand, 15 other states had moved forward in the direction of introducing the legislation.“Our government will implement the UCC in all the states governed by our party,” he said.Congress top leaders review preparations in poll-bound states of Manipur and UttarakhandUttarakhand became the first state in the country to implement the UCC in January 2025. The legislation provides a common framework for personal laws governing matters such as marriage, divorce and inheritance.Shah also asked party leaders and workers to intensify their outreach ahead of the elections scheduled early next year, seeking a third consecutive term for the BJP in the state.“Last time, you gave us 47 seats. But this time, we have to move forward with the target of 65-plus seats,” Shah said, referring to the BJP’s performance in the 2022 Assembly elections.The BJP had won 57 seats in the 2017 Assembly elections and 47 in 2022 in the 70-member Uttarakhand Assembly.Shah said the BJP wanted to make Uttarakhand a “secure and prosperous” state and transform Devbhoomi into the country’s “cultural capital”.The home minister also targeted the Congress, accusing it of leaving Uttarakhand dependent on a “money-order economy” and migration, while claiming that the BJP had worked to establish an industrial economy in the state.He highlighted infrastructure projects, including the Delhi-Dehradun economic corridor and the Rishikesh-Karnaprayag railway line, and said the government had undertaken efforts to curb migration from border villages.The home minister also attacked Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his “Vote Bachao Yatra”, alleging that it was actually a “Ghuspaithiya Bachao Yatra”.Shah said BJP workers would reach out to people across the state and seek their support for the party’s third consecutive term.

stories.primary_headline: If Dune is this generation’s Star Wars, we are all in big trouble

primary_source.headline: If Dune is this generation’s Star Wars, we are all in big trouble
primary_source.content: According to Florence Pugh, Denis Villeneuve’s stunningly strange and breathtaking universe is the equivalent to George Lucas’ heroic space opera. Let’s hope notA long time ago, far far away, in a galaxy called the 1970s, kids dreamed of joining the rebellion, rescuing a princess and blowing up the Death Star. Peer into the cosmic tea leaves and it would become immediately clear that no amount of evildoing could withstand a neurotic gold butler, a dustbin with ideas above its station and a walking seven-foot tall shagpile carpet with a very low tolerance for disagreement.It is worth remembering this when considering Florence Pugh’s recent declaration, ahead of next month’s Dune: Part Three, that Dune is her generation’s Star Wars. And then wondering how much trouble we might be in if she’s actually right. “I think they brought back movie-going. What an event the second [Dune] was,” Pugh cheerfully told the New York Times. “It was just so lovely to be a part of something that we know is our generational kind of Star Wars.” Continue reading...

brief_bullets: Actor Florence Pugh recently declared Denis Villeneuve’s cinematic adaptation of Dune to be her generation’s equivalent to Star Wars, praising its monumental impact on reviving theatrical movie-going. While George Lucas’s original space opera offered a clear dichotomy of heroic rebellion, whimsical sidekicks, and triumphant victories, Villeneuve’s franchise presents a stunningly strange, morally ambiguous universe defined by geopolitical ruthlessness and existential dread. This stark thematic shift highlights a profound cultural pivot from optimistic escapism toward darker, more complex cinematic narratives that mirror contemporary anxieties.
why_it_matters_bullets: It signals a cultural transition toward darker, morally ambiguous cinema shaping modern generational identity.

stories.primary_headline: True North by Paul Theroux review – an American’s view of Canada

primary_source.headline: True North by Paul Theroux review – an American’s view of Canada
primary_source.content: The veteran travel writer turns his eye for detail on his northern neighbour and its peoplePaul Theroux’s arrival in Canada doesn’t go well. An immigration officer called Sweeney finds a small pocketknife in his car and fines him $500 for failing to declare a weapon. “I’m going to make you famous,” he angrily tells her, stumping up. Maybe he will, with this book. Canadians are reputed to be polite and easygoing, “slaves to their courtesy”, but the country has changed enormously in recent years. Will Theroux find it stuffed with Sweeney-ites? Luckily the answer is no.He issues a warning that, after 11 previous travel books, this may be his last; global overtourism appals him and so does much travel writing. But he shares Jack Kerouac’s delight in being on the road, and from his home in Massachusetts it’s just a four-hour drive to the border. His purpose is less to check out “the strangers next door” than to visit the village of Yamaska, in Quebec. It was there that a Frenchman called Antoine Theroux settled in the 17th century; a dozen or more Theroux families still live there; one local street is called Rue Theroux. The author isn’t only made welcome but presented with a certificate of honour by the local mayor. He repays the honour with a long chapter of family history. Continue reading...

sources.headline: True North by Paul Theroux review – an American’s view of Canada

brief_bullets: Renowned travel writer Paul Theroux explores Canada in his latest work, True North, which he suggests may be his final travelogue due to his growing disillusionment with global overtourism. The narrative begins with a contentious border crossing involving a fine for an undeclared knife, yet quickly pivots to a deeply personal journey as Theroux travels from Massachusetts to Yamaska, Quebec. Seeking his ancestral roots, he discovers a thriving community of his namesakes and receives an official certificate of honor from the local mayor. By blending historical research with contemporary observations, Theroux challenges stereotypes about Canadian politeness while reflecting on the evolving nature of his craft and the complexities of national identity in the modern era.
why_it_matters_bullets: Theroux’s potential retirement from travel writing signals a broader cultural shift in how authors critique the ethics of tourism.

primary_source.headline: Wipro appoints Angan Guha as President and CEO for Americas 2 Strategic Market Unit
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: Wipro Limited on Friday announced the appointment of Angan Guha as President and Chief Executive Officer for Americas 2 Strategic Market Unit, effective December 8, 2026. He will report to the CEO and Managing Director, Srini Pallia, and serve on the Wipro Executive Leadership Team.In this role, Guha will focus on strengthening the business and market momentum across BFSI, Energy & Utilities, and Manufacturing, and accelerating growth, deepen client relationships, and deliver greater value to our clients in the region.Wipro headcount falls by 6,716 in Q2, biggest decline in recent quarters“We are delighted to welcome Angan to Wipro’s leadership team,” said Srini Pallia, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of Wipro Limited. “His experience in driving business growth, combined with his focus on innovation and execution, will be valuable as we strengthen our Americas business. I am confident that his leadership will help us accelerate growth, deepen client relationships, and deliver greater value to our clients," he added.“The evolving AI landscape presents unprecedented opportunities for businesses to innovate and lead. I look forward to collaborating with the talented team at Wipro and helping clients navigate this transformation, drive meaningful business outcomes, and build on Wipro’s strong consulting and technology capabilities,"&nbsp;Angan Guha said.Guha is an experienced technology and business leader who has spent more than three decades driving growth, digital transformation and client success across BFSI, Energy & Utilities and Manufacturing, Wipro said. Prior to serving as Global CEO & Managing Director of Birlasoft Ltd., Guha spent over 28 years at Wipro, holding several senior leadership roles, including CEO of the Americas 2 Business Unit and member of Wipro’s Leadership Team.

stories.primary_headline: 1,800 dubious books, inflated prices: Periyar library row triggers DMK-TVK blame game

primary_source.headline: 1,800 dubious books, inflated prices: Periyar library row triggers DMK-TVK blame game
primary_source.content: Chennai: No one in Tamil literary circles has ever heard of Agalvilakku Pathipagam. But the hitherto unknown publication house has supplied about 1,800 books to the Periyar Arivulagam, a modern library built at a cost of Rs 300 crore in Coimbatore, inaugurated by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay in October.The procurement of never-heard-of books from a dubious publication house has raised questions of a mega scam in buying books for the library, a pet project of former Chief Minister M K Stalin. The alleged scam came to light after acclaimed Tamil author Perumal Murugan, whose brilliant works have been translated into English and other languages, visited the library in Coimbatore and found these books on the racks on the fourth floor."Whatever the case may be, it is certain that a massive scam has taken place in the procurement of books. New publishing houses have been started solely to supply books to this library. Books have been generated using artificial intelligence with outdated technology,” he alleged in an article on Sindhai, a Tamil magazine.&nbsp;‘Exorbitant prices’The contents of the books supplied by the publication house in question are mostly generated using artificial intelligence (AI), containing false information and distorted facts about the history of Tamil Nadu, and were procured at exorbitant rates.For instance, a 300-page book titled Naladiyar: Vaazhvin Vazhikaati is priced at Rs 1,445. To top it all, Agalvilakku Pathipagam functions from an apartment in Madipakkam, a locality in Chennai, and its owner refused to speak to the media.Moreover, some of the authors whose books have been procured have never been heard of, and their names sound fake, such as Trisha Vijay, Thamarai Karthi, Madhu Sakthi, Malathi Sethuraman, and Keerthi Govind. Other interesting names of authors of books published by Agalvilakku Pathipagam that still adorn the library racks are Vijay Balu, Vijay Selvam, Vijay Adithan, and Sumega Vijay.Data quoted by the Information Integrity Desk (IID) — the TN Government’s fact-check unit — shows that all 2,393 books published by the publications with names of authors were registered between December 3, 2024, and February 6, 2026. A total of 609 author names, including the name Trisha Vijay, were also registered.Murugan, who was also part of the committee with over 100 members to recommend books for the library, demanded that the books be removed from the shelves immediately to ensure books with distorted facts don’t find space.Tamil Nadu CM slams DMK, says author Perumal Murugan exposed graft in buying books during its regime How did this happen?While the committee with over 100 members from various genres of the literary field was constituted in November 2025 under the then DMK government to suggest books to be purchased for the library, documents seen by DH show the books were delivered to the library between March 2026 and June 2026 — during the transition period, including the Assembly elections and after TVK assumed office.Questions remain on how these dubious books were bought by the library without checking, and when the School Education Department issued the order for the said publication. Except for Agalvilakku Pathipagam, other books in the library are of good standards.As expected, the allegations of a scam set off a blame game between the DMK and TVK. Interestingly, Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay took to his X page as TVK chief to deride the DMK as the “most corrupt party,” which didn’t even spare a library in the name of Periyar.&nbsp;The DMK hit back at the CM for blaming the party and demanded an impartial investigation — it alleged that only books procured from the said publication and another were received at the library in June 2026. Other opposition parties also strongly condemned inclusion of dubious books in a world-class library. &nbsp;‘Members were asked recommendations’DH spoke to a couple of members of the committee who said the orders for procurement of books were issued online and members were asked for recommendations only on the subjects they were experts in.&nbsp;“We were asked about the books to be bought in a particular stream and we gave our recommendations. We were not aware of who got the orders. Not all members were consulted on all subjects. Every stream had a set of experts and professors,” a member said.Another member said some of the procured books, which he was informed about, were of “good standard” and will help library visitors.Conceived by the previous DMK government, the construction of the swanky library spread over an area of about 2 lakh square feet was almost complete when the TVK assumed office in May 2026—the former Chief Minister said recently his predecessor just cut the ribbons.Murugan’s sarcasmMurugan said he had never heard of Agalvilakku Pathipagam in his 40 years of experience as a writer. “It appears that my world of reading and search for knowledge has become so narrow,” he wrote sarcastically.Naladiyar: Vaazhvin Vazhikaati is another book that caught Murugan’s attention, not just for its exorbitant price of Rs 1,445 for 350 pages but also for its false content. The book describes Naladiyar — a classical Tamil Jain poetic work — as one of the important poets and philosophers in Tamil.&nbsp;“I have been teaching Tamil for three decades, but I never learned that Naladiyar was a philosopher,” he added.Turning the tables on the DMK, the IID said a GO was issued on November 5, 2025 constituting a committee to procure books worth Rs 50 crore for the library and on January 9, 2026, the committee selected books for procurement following which negotiations were held on January 24.&nbsp;“Based on this, approval was obtained at a high-level committee meeting held on 05.02.2026 to place orders for the selected books.&nbsp;Subsequently, on 06.02.2026, the coordinating committee for special libraries recommended a list of books and issued a purchase order for their procurement. Accordingly, 60,266 books worth Rs 19.19 crore were procured for the Periyar Knowledge Centre,” the IID said.&nbsp;

brief_bullets: A major political controversy has erupted in Tamil Nadu following revelations that Coimbatore's newly inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam library procured nearly 1,800 artificially generated and overpriced books from an obscure publisher, Agalvilakku Pathipagam. Acclaimed author Perumal Murugan exposed the acquisition of volumes featuring fictitious authors and distorted historical facts, prompting fierce political friction between Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay and the opposition DMK regarding procurement corruption during the transition period. The scandal has intensified scrutiny over institutional oversight, forcing authorities to address compromised literary standards and allegations of financial graft in high-profile public infrastructure projects.
why_it_matters_bullets: This procurement scandal exposes systemic vulnerabilities in state-funded cultural projects, threatening political credibility and demanding stricter oversight.

stories.primary_headline: India, EU conclude multi-billion Euro global innovation programme

primary_source.headline: India, EU conclude multi-billion Euro global innovation programme
primary_source.content: New Delhi: India and the European Union have concluded negotiations on New Delhi's association with a Euro 93.5 billion flagship research and innovation programme, paving the way for expanded collaboration under their broader strategic partnership.The decision comes weeks before India and the 27-nation bloc are set to seal a landmark free trade agreement -- billed as the "mother of all deals" -- to create a market of two billion people.The European Commission and India have successfully concluded negotiations on New Delhi's association to Horizon Europe programme, the EU said.American midterm results will not have an impact on India-US interim  trade deal: SourcesThis marks an important step forward for EU-India relations, strengthening scientific cooperation, creating new opportunities in research, and deepening the strategic partnership, it said.India's association with the Horizon programme is seen as part of the comprehensive strategic agenda of the two sides for the next five years.For researchers, businesses and research organisations across Europe, India's association will open up more opportunities to collaborate with Indian partners and build lasting scientific and technological links, the EU said.Once the agreement is signed and the necessary procedures are completed on both sides, researchers and organisations in India will be able to receive funding directly from Horizon Europe and lead collaborative projects under its Pillar II: 'Global Challenges and European Industrial Competitiveness', it said.This is the largest part of the programme which funds collaborative, multi-national research and innovation projects tackling societal and technological issues, such as health, digital, industry, space, climate, energy, and bioeconomy.The EU said the move will create new opportunities for European and Indian partners to pool expertise, develop technologies and address shared challenges.Association is the closest form of cooperation offered by the EU to non-EU countries under Horizon Europe.It allows organisations in associated countries to participate on equal terms with their EU counterparts in the parts of the programme covered by the agreement. In return, associated countries contribute financially to the programme.The successful conclusion of negotiations clears the way for the signature of the association agreement, subject to the completion of the necessary procedures on both sides. The two sides are likely to sign the formal agreement in January.India and the EU had launched the exploratory discussions on the Horizon programme in February 2026 and formal negotiations began in July.EU-India scientific cooperation builds on the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation, signed in 2001 and renewed until 2030.Research and innovation also form an integral part of the Joint EU-India Comprehensive Strategic Agenda towards 2030, adopted at the summit talks between the two sides in New Delhi on January 27.The partnership has been strengthened through the EU-India Trade and Technology Council, which facilitates collaboration on key digital areas such as artificial intelligence, digital public infrastructure, semiconductors, high-performance computing, digital skills and the sixth generation of wireless telecommunications.The EU and India took a further step in collaboration on digital skills through the launch of the first-ever European Legal Gateway Office in India last February, aiming to facilitate safe, legal and well-informed mobility to the EU in the ICT sector.Horizon Europe runs from 2021 to 2027, with a budget of Euro 93.5 billion.International cooperation is central to the programme, bringing together expertise and resources to advance scientific excellence and innovation.Currently, 23 non-EU countries are associated with Horizon Europe. They are: Albania, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Canada, Egypt, the Faroe Islands, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Japan, Korea, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Serbia, Switzerland, TÃ¼rkiye, Tunisia, Ukraine and the United Kingdom.The India and EU ties have witnessed a major upswing in the last few years.The two sides are set to sign the free trade deal next month.

brief_bullets: India and the European Union have successfully concluded negotiations for New Delhi's association with the Euro 93.5 billion Horizon Europe research and innovation initiative. Driven by the European Commission and Indian authorities, this agreement allows Indian researchers and institutions to directly receive funding and lead collaborative projects tackling critical global challenges like climate change, health, and digital technology. Arriving just ahead of a projected landmark free trade agreement encompassing two billion people, this milestone significantly deepens bilateral scientific cooperation and fortifies the broader strategic partnership between both major democratic powers.
why_it_matters_bullets: This partnership accelerates joint technological innovation and consolidates geopolitical ties ahead of a massive bilateral trade agreement.
